about: The demo's GETs board, invented: the group experiential themes across Juno's, Rowan's and Mabel's PETs. Each GET by its title, with its description, its PETs and sub-PETs, each named by its participant and its title, and the quote ticked for each participant's row of the GET table, in that participant's words. Every PET and sub-PET of the three is named once, under a GET or set aside, a sub-PET set aside where its PET carries it. make_demo.py builds idiograph-gets.json from this and the three cases' boards.

gets.title: A home come alive with the dog, and gone flat without her
gets.description: Lights on again for Mabel, a house never empty for Juno until two hours at the groomer's, and for Rowan arms with nothing to hold and a flat that is just a flat

members.pet: “Like having the lights on”: the house alive again
The dog at the centre of home, felt most in her absence
Her absence lived in his body and his flat

quotes.Mabel: It's like having the lights on. That's the nearest I can get to it.
quotes.Juno: I suppose she is just there. That is the first thing. Bramble is just there, all the time. … The house is never empty now. Even when it is quiet it is not empty.
quotes.Rowan: I just felt very light, like my arms didn't have anything to hold. And then I drove home, and the flat was, it was just a flat.

gets.title: The dog a way back to people, or a way round them
gets.description: Mabel back among people on the green, Rowan cut off behind a reason nobody argues with, and Juno finding the dog easier than the people at home

members.pet: Needed again, and out among people without trying
A life closed in round her fear, unnoticed
Finding “the dog is easier” than the people at home, and uneasy about it

quotes.Mabel: It's lovely. I don't want to overdo it, but it's saved me a bit. … I'd lost the habit. You forget how. And with a dog you don't need to know how … the talking just happens round the edges.
quotes.Rowan: I'd stopped saying yes to things so long ago that people had stopped asking. So it's hard to say what it was like, because I didn't feel it as a loss while it was going on. … The dog was the reason, and it's a good reason, nobody argues with it.
quotes.Juno: The dog is easier. That is the thing I keep landing on and then moving off, because it is not a nice thing to think about yourself. She does not need me to have got anything right.

gets.title: Changed by the dog in ways none of them saw coming
gets.description: Juno caught going soft, Mabel opened out of a shut-in life and Rowan taken over, each changed before they saw it happen, and each in a different direction

members.pet: “Caught” going soft for the dog she said no to
“Shut in” after Dennis died, until the dog opened the door
The best company he has had, in a life “arranged round her”

quotes.Juno: It is like being caught. I am not a soppy person, or I did not think I was. … And I have started groaning back at her. That is the state of me now.
quotes.Mabel: Only that I didn't expect it. Any of it. … She opened the door, really, that's what it is. I was shut in and she opened the door. Some mornings I'd still rather she hadn't, when it's sleeting. But mostly I'm glad.
quotes.Rowan: But the other way is that she took over. Everything had to be arranged round her. Every single thing. And I didn't see it happening until it had already happened.

gets.title: Holding on to the dog through what it costs, or letting her go
gets.description: Mabel keeps Pepper through a fall and her daughter's fears, Juno through a regret never said and a night that cost her, and Rowan gives Skye up and takes the fault as his

members.pet: Holding on to Pepper, and to her own say over her life
A first year's regret, too terrible to say and never quite gone
A wordless closeness, proved by what it costs her
Giving her up, and not knowing “whether I failed her”

quotes.Mabel: I didn't sleep much. But I knew I wasn't giving her up. I knew that by the morning.
quotes.Juno: I think because it cost me something. That sounds a bit grand. But the easy days do not prove anything, do they.
quotes.Rowan: Awful. And a relief. Both at once, and I was ashamed of the relief, I still am a bit.

gets.title: The parting from the dog, faced ahead of time or still unsettled after
gets.description: Juno finds her grief rehearsed on a false alarm, Mabel provides for a dog likely to outlive her, and Rowan, three months on, still keeps Skye in his body and his cupboard

members.pet: Home “never empty” with the dog, and its loss already rehearsed
Lighter for knowing Pepper will not be left waiting when she dies
Still holding on to a dog he let go

quotes.Juno: She had a thorn in her foot and I had spent twenty minutes organising my own grief in advance, in traffic. … So that Saturday was a rehearsal. And I did not enjoy finding out that I have got the whole thing ready to go.
quotes.Mabel: When I go to the shops she's at the window when I come back. Every time. … And I couldn't bear the thought of her doing that and me never coming.
quotes.Rowan: That's the strange bit. … I was halfway across before I thought, what are you doing, you haven't got a dog. My body was still doing it for her.

set_aside.pet: Drawn home by a welcome nobody else gives her
A morning grievance the dog takes away unsaid
Half nine: closer through the dog, or talking about her “instead of talking”
Grief for the dog rehearsed on a false alarm, then pushed away
Won over against her picture of herself
A walk once resented, now “the bit of the day that is mine”
Letting her go, with a relief he is ashamed of
The fault taken as his, never the dog's
Glad for her, and still unsettled three months on
Her bowl, her sock and her good name, kept
Company and peace in a lonely time
